title: Type Safety in CuTe DSL
critical_patterns: Always annotate kernel parameters to ensure compile-time error checking
Use specific scalar types like cutlass.Int32 instead of Python int
Explicit casts are preferred for type conversions to avoid precision loss
Type specialization allows different kernels for different tensor dtypes
code_snippets:

constraints: Type annotations are mandatory for all kernel parameters
Compile-time constants must be marked with cutlass.Constexpr
Tensor types must be cute.Tensor, not torch.Tensor
Type mismatches are caught at compile time, preventing runtime errors
Implicit conversions may lead to precision loss and should be handled carefully
compressed_summary: CuTe DSL emphasizes type safety through mandatory type annotations for kernel parameters, enabling compile-time error detection and optimization. Strong typing ensures that errors are caught early, improving performance and code clarity. Key types include cute.Tensor for tensors and cutlass.Int32, cutlass.Float32 for scalars, with cutlass.Constexpr used for compile-time constants. Type inference is applied to return types and local variables, but explicit annotations are required for function parameters. Compile-time type checking prevents common errors like using incorrect types for array indices or mismatched function arguments. Type conversions should be explicit to avoid precision loss, and type specialization allows for optimized kernel compilation based on tensor dtypes. Best practices include always annotating parameters, using specific CuTe types over Python types, and employing Constexpr for values known at compile time. Runtime type validation is also recommended to ensure tensor compatibility before kernel execution. The document provides practical patterns and code snippets to guide developers in writing efficient and error-free GPU kernels with CuTe DSL.
